title: PTC-assisted sustainable synthesis and integrated  in silico  evaluation of novel 2-oxo-nicotinonitrile derivatives as multitarget larvicidal agents against  Culex pipiens  L
content: This study reports an operationally efficient and mild phase-transfer catalytic (PTC) synthesis of novel 2-oxo nicotinonitrile derivatives as potential larvicidal agents against Culex pipiens L. Compared with conventional reflux, the PTC protocol afforded markedly higher yields of 73–95% within 6–10 h, whereas the thermal method gave only 16–23% yields after 19–24 h. Larvicidal evaluation against third-instar larvae identified compounds 8, 2b, 10, and 4 as the most active derivatives, with LC50 values of 7.65, 9.92, 10.48, and 10.48 µg mL−1, respectively. Although their potency was lower than that of pyriproxyfen, these compounds showed promising activity as newly synthesized lead candidates. Molecular docking against Lymnaea stagnalis acetylcholine-binding protein and Aedes aegypti juvenile hormone-binding protein revealed favorable interactions consistent with a possible multitarget mode of action. DFT calculations showed that compound 8 possessed the lowest HOMO–LUMO energy gap and hardness and the highest softness among the synthesized candidates, supporting its superior activity within the series. SAR analysis highlighted the importance of molecular rigidity, substituent size, and hydrogen-bonding capacity. Compounds 4 and 8 also showed favorable predicted ADME and toxicity profiles, including lack of blood–brain barrier penetration, acceptable bioavailability, and relatively high LD50 values. Overall, PTC provides an operationally efficient and high-yielding route to biologically active nicotinonitrile derivatives, with compound 8 emerging as the most promising larvicidal lead.
